_expect.name: Back Porch slabs and Jump Back Rock, The

az_back_porch_slabs_and_jump_back_rock_t.blurb: A small bouldering zone inside the Main Boulders section of Groom Creek, on the hillside south of Prescott at roughly 6,000 feet. It holds ten problems, all on the easy end: most are around V0, with a couple at V1. The name hints at the style, since the Back Porch is a set of friendly slabs, and Jump Back Rock adds a few more problems nearby. Granite boulders around here are coarse and grippy, with sloping and crimpy holds, so tough skin helps. The surroundings are partly wooded with plenty of sun reaching the rocks. It suits beginners, warm-ups and anyone looking for low-grade problems before heading to the harder boulders elsewhere in Groom Creek.

az_insomnia_west.blurb: Insomnia West is the west rim of Insomnia Canyon, a deep, sheer Coconino sandstone slot feeding into the West Fork of Oak Creek north of Sedona. The ten climbs here are mainly trad, with one sport line and a short aid pitch, and the grades run from about 5.9 up through the low 5.12s, so it is a place for strong, experienced parties. Several lines are long multi-pitch crack routes in clean sandstone. Getting to the cliff is a commitment: the walk is rough, overgrown and in places burned, and some sections are reached by descending from the rim. Expect solitude rather than crowds.

az_beach_the_2.blurb: The Beach is a small sport crag in La Milagrosa Canyon, where the Santa Catalinas rise from the edge of Tucson. Its profile resembles a breaking wave: gently overhanging on one end, steepening to a heavily overhung section at the other. All ten routes are bolted and hard, mostly 5.12 with a pair of 5.11s and a few 5.13s, so it is not a spot for newer leaders. The wall picks up early sun and gets hot in direct light, which makes late-winter and early-spring afternoons the comfortable time to visit. Expect steep, sustained, powerful climbing.

az_tralfamadore_wall.blurb: One of the main walls on the North Side of Volunteer Canyon, in the Sycamore Canyon country west of Flagstaff, around 6,600 feet. All ten routes here are trad, mostly 5.9 to 5.10 with one easier and one harder outlier. The wall offers some of the longest, cleanest moderate lines in Volunteer, with a few climbs stretching nearly a full rope length. A distinctive jagged roof is the landmark when you walk the rim. Lines were once climbed as multi-pitch from the canyon floor, but today are often done as long single pitches from ledges above the base. The North Side faces south, so spring and fall are best.

az_timmies_west.blurb: Timmies West is a sizeable formation in Lower Sullivan Canyon, a pocketed basalt canyon a few miles north of Chino Valley in central Arizona. It forms its own tier above the Opera House area, divided from the lower routes by a band of scree. All ten climbs are trad, spanning roughly 5.6 to 5.11, with most in the 5.9 to 5.10 range and several well-rated crack lines. There are no fixed anchors on this wall, so plan to bring your own gear to build them, and carry a full rack. The canyon is a good choice for crack climbers wanting uncrowded, steep lines.

az_san_pedro_wall.blurb: A granite crag in the Mid-Mountain stretch of the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon, above Tucson. The ten routes are all trad, ranging from easy fifth class up to 5.10-, with the bulk in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, which makes it a friendly place for moderate leaders. Rock quality is mostly excellent. The setting is quiet and a bit removed, with views over the valley, and there is little shade but a steady breeze usually drifts across the face. Reaching the base takes a trail walk of about a quarter hour plus a loose descent down a gully. Bring a standard trad rack.

az_lost_in_the_woods_wall.blurb: A wall in the Pit, the pocketed limestone sport crag east of Flagstaff, at about 6,700 feet. Ten bolted lines range from 5.8 through the 5.12s, with most falling between 5.10 and 5.12, so there is a mix for solid intermediates and stronger climbers alike. It tends to be quieter than the busier sections of the Pit. Expect aging gear: some bolts are rusted, anchors are a mix of chains and cold shuts, and first bolts often sit high enough that a stick clip earns its place. The wall is reached by following a trail along the base of the cliffs, starting from the Son Tower.

az_octopus_s_garden.blurb: A small east-facing cirque just northwest of Midgley Bridge outside Sedona, where ten bolted sport climbs sit on a prominent bench above the canyon. Routes run from very easy up to the low 5.10s, with most in the 5.6 to 5.10 range, making it one of the better beginner and moderate sport options near town. The cirque catches mostly sun, so it is pleasant in cooler months and warm otherwise. The walk starts from the Midgley Bridge area on the Jim Thompson trail and finishes on a small use trail up a ridge to a ledge, then a short stroll along it. Slab and face climbing in a scenic setting.

_conflicts.az_octopus_s_garden: Stored rock is limestone; the parent Midgley Bridge Area page describes the crags as on a step of sandstone (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105808423/midgley-bridge-area); the crag's own page (https://mountainproject.com/area/118311284/octopuss-garden) names no rock. Stored value left unchanged and rock not named in blurb.
